observations.label: A FOURTH temporal gap class -- an EVENT-BOUNDED INTERVAL has no v1 form, and no §8 tag exists for it
observations.status: RECORDED, NOT TAGGED, NOT MEASURED. Reviewer ruling 2026-09-24. Queued as §10.1 F25.
observations.note:
AN EVENT-BOUNDED INTERVAL HAS NO v1 TEMPORAL FORM, AND NO SECTION 8 TAG EXISTS FOR IT. Recorded here rather than resolved inside an annotation pass, the same way E02-006#calendar-days-unit-gap was logged before F23 and C04-051#temporal-composition / C04-072#temporal-composition were logged before F21. Carried by locked item C10-03.

THE PHRASE: 'during the pendency of such challenge' (inside C10-03's span).

THE MECHANISM, NAMED PRECISELY SO A FUTURE SESSION DOES NOT RE-DERIVE IT, AND ESTABLISHED BY READING ast.py RATHER THAN THE REGEX. DuringTemporal is {start: DateRef, end: DateRef} -- A DATE PAIR. The interval here is bounded not by two dates but by the PENDENCY OF AN EVENT: it begins when a challenge is filed and ends when that challenge is resolved, and neither bound is a date the contract states or that any surface rewriting could supply. There is NO SLOT for an event-bounded interval in the form at all. Confirmed by execution through the production _classify_temporal(), gated first on a known accept ('within 3 days of receipt of the data' -> WITHIN 3d OF "...") and a known reject, per Standing Principle 7: 'during the pendency of such challenge' -> None, and so is 'during the pendency of the challenge' and the bare 'during the Term'.

THEREFORE REPRESENTATIONAL, NOT REACHABILITY -- section 8.6.1's test, applied rather than assumed. This is NOT a surface pattern rejecting input the IR could hold (which is what within_parenthetical and within_preposition are, and why section 8.13 and section 8.6 annotate the FORM). The IR cannot hold it. So section 8.6.1's principle puts `temporal: null` here, and that is the null it licenses -- 'null marks what the IR cannot REPRESENT, never what the classifier cannot REACH'.

DISTINCT FROM BOTH EXISTING TEMPORAL GAP TAGS, checked against each rather than assumed novel:
  NOT `temporal_composition` (section 8.12, F21) -- that gap is a SLOT gap, several temporal elements against ast.Obligation's single `temporal` field. HERE THERE IS EXACTLY ONE ELEMENT. It is a FORM gap, not a slot gap.
  NOT `lead_time_unrepresentable` (section 8.11, F19) -- that gap is a DURATION paired with a DIRECTION ('at least 30 days before X'), which no v1 form pairs. HERE THERE IS NEITHER a duration nor a direction.
  Its nearest structural sibling is section 8.11 (both are single-form expressiveness failures), not section 8.12.

DELIBERATELY NOT MINTED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT MEASURED POOL-WIDE HERE. Section 22.1's discipline: a kind is not ruled on a sample of one. F23 is the direct precedent -- the calendar-days unit gap was recorded and left untagged on exactly this reasoning. A corpus-wide sweep of the class is real section 10 investigation work and belongs in its own session if and when a second instance appears; running it inside an annotation pass would bundle a measurement decision into an item's drafting. REVIEWER-RULED 2026-09-24. Queued as section 10.1 F25.

THE COST IS REAL AND IS STATED RATHER THAN LEFT LATENT, because it runs the OPPOSITE way to most untagged gaps. With `known_gaps` EMPTY, C10-03 ENTERS section 9.1's kind-scoped in-force criterion-2 denominator -- an untagged item is a scoreable item -- while carrying a temporal IR v1 provably cannot represent. It is therefore likely a GUARANTEED failure in the headline denominator: an extractor that quotes the phrase into `temporal_raw` gets UNMAPPABLE_TEMPORAL and the WHOLE candidate is rejected, which is section 15.3's LOUD side (the placement section 15.3 itself got wrong and v0.34 corrected). Latent today only because C10-025 has no cassette, so report.py's G8 discloses the item as cassette-unscoreable. This is the strongest argument for minting the tag at a second instance, and it is priced here so the next session does not re-argue it.

FORCING FUNCTION: a second independent instance of an event-bounded interval. Most informative would be one in a segment that IS cassette-backed, since that would convert the cost above from latent to measured.

SEARCH KEY: event-bounded interval, pendency, DuringTemporal, DateRef pair, temporal form gap, F25, C10-025, C10-03, section 8.11, section 8.12.
